title: Modeling the Sacred: Considerations when Using Religious Texts in Natural Language Processing
religious_groups: Church of Jesus Christ of the Latter Day Saints (LDS)
models_tested: No specific LLMs were evaluated in this paper.
findings: The paper finds that thousands of NLP research papers use religious texts, especially the Bible and Quran, due to their wide availability and multilingual nature. This use is heavily biased towards Abrahamic religions. The research community often treats these texts simply as data, overlooking their sacred nature, cultural context, and problematic provenance, which can be entwined with colonial and proselytizing efforts. The most common application is machine translation, particularly for low-resource languages. The paper argues for greater ethical consideration, including researcher positionality and engagement with religious and marginalized communities, when using such texts.

measurement_description: This paper does not introduce a benchmark for LLMs. Instead, it conducts an empirical study and meta-analysis of the ACL Anthology to measure how, why, and which religious texts (primarily the Bible and Quran) are used as data in NLP research, particularly for tasks like machine translation and dataset creation.
